sources.entry: Zettel - Minimal, distraction-free note-taking app with Markdown and hashtag-based organization. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/AlexW00/Zettel) [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/app/zettel-quick-notes/id6748525244?platform=mac)

summary.one_liner: Zettel is a minimal, distraction-free local note-taking app for iPhone and Mac that stores notes as Markdown files and organizes them with hashtags.
summary.what_it_does: The app offers a single-note focus mode with a full-screen editing interface, so only one note is edited at a time. Notes are organized with hashtag tags (#tag). Users can choose light, dark, or system themes. All notes are stored as simple Markdown files. The README describes it as a local app, and the repository includes Xcode build scripts for iOS and macOS, with configuration driven by a .env file containing Apple Developer details.
use_cases: distraction-free note taking on iPhone and Mac
writing single notes in full-screen mode
keeping plain Markdown notes as local files
building the Zettel app from source with Xcode
how_to_run: Alternatively run ./configure.sh, then build in Xcode or with xcodebuild
stack: Swift (implied by Xcode project; not named in README)
notable: Notes are plain Markdown files, so they remain readable outside the app
Build scripts configure the Xcode project from a .env file
caveats: Building from source requires an Apple Developer Team ID and bundle identifier
Official download is through the App Store; the README gives no separate binary release
